input.rationale: Submitted the focused probe harness that drives a 5-replica configuration through a phase-2 acceptance of X on instance (0,0), a leader crash after the Accept broadcast, and a recovery of that instance by a replica that holds no command for it. Local native feedback reproduced the predicted witness (recovery proposed a NOOP although the quorum reply carried the PUT at vbal 0, and the NOOP then committed at the live replicas, erasing X at its only live holder); the formal account still needs the controller's receipt, so the interpretation remains conditional.

scope.description: Five replicas (F=2) constructed in-process with the package's own field and RPC-table initialization, without peer sockets and without the run() loop, so handler execution is deterministic. All inter-replica traffic is the package's own marshaled RPC structs: each bcast runs SendMsg into a captured byte buffer and every delivery decodes a fresh object from those bytes, preserving the transport serialization boundary; delivery is FIFO per link and messages to a crashed replica are dropped. The executed scenario is: replica 1 pre-accepts a conflicting command on its own instance (2,0); leader replica 0 proposes X (PUT key 1) on instance (0,0); replica 1 replies non-equal then crashes; replica 0 runs the Accept phase at ballot 0 to replicas 2 and 3; replica 0 crashes after the Accept broadcast and before consuming any AcceptReply; replica 3 (which received only the Accept, holds no command, and has crtInstance[0] == 0) calls startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) as its own executor would after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD; the quiescent message exchange is then completed.
assumptions: Replica construction mirrors epaxos.New minus peer connections, the run() loop and ComputeClosestPeers, so PreferredPeerOrder is the constructor order (id+1+i) mod N.
InstanceSpace rows hold 32 entries instead of MAX_INSTANCE (10M); only instances 0..2 are used, so no code path indexes beyond the allocated row.

The auxiliary broadcast of replica 1's conflicting proposal is discarded; only its local conflict state (conflicts[2][key 1]) is used as the premise that makes the leader's pre-accept reply non-equal and therefore forces the Accept phase.

Crashes are modelled as: the replica stops consuming messages, no further message is delivered to it, and every other replica's Alive flag for it is cleared, matching the target's mechanism for deciding broadcast recipients.
Replica 3's recovery is invoked through startRecoveryForInstance, the same function the target's executor invokes from instancesToRecover after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD.
excluded: No client connection path, no execution of the state machine, no recovery timer loop, and no master/BeTheLeader designation (IsLeader stays false, as epaxos.New sets it).

experiment.prefix: The harness builds five in-process replicas, injects the conflicting premise at replica 1, runs replica 0's proposal of X through the package's own startPhase1/bcastPreAccept/handlePreAcceptReply/bcastAccept path, delivers the Accept to replicas 2 and 3, crashes replicas 1 and 0, then calls replica 3's startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) and delivers the resulting Prepare/PrepareReply traffic through the package's own handlePrepare/handlePrepareReply. Every outgoing message is decoded from the bytes SendMsg flushed, so message content, ballot fields and commands are the target's own values.
experiment.requirement: A recovery of instance (0,0) must not replace with a different value the value that the collected prepare replies report as accepted or pre-accepted; the recovering coordinator adopts the value carried at the highest value ballot among the replies (including its own state) and re-proposes that value if it must restart phase 1.
experiment.responsibility: The recovering coordinator's own adoption rule (epaxos/epaxos.go:1236-1313) and startRecoveryForInstance's construction of its self reply (epaxos/epaxos.go:1142-1168), not the client or the environment: the leader's crash after broadcasting Accept is a permitted failure, and the value X was accepted at ballot 0 by replicas 0, 2 and 3 in the executed scenario.

comparisons.description: The command the recovery proposes for instance (0,0) equals the PUT carried by the prepare reply with the highest value ballot (the quorum-held value X); violated when the recovered PreAccept carries the NOOP (cmd_op 0) although quorum_reply_command_op is 1.

A replica that held X after the Accept phase still holds X once the recovered proposal has run to quiescence; violated when the live holder ends up with the NOOP (cmd_op 0) because the recovered PreAccept overwrote its command.

materials.text:
inst.lb = r.newLeaderBookkeepingDefault()
	lb := inst.lb
	lb.clientProposals = proposals
	lb.ballot = inst.vbal
	lb.seq = inst.Seq
	lb.cmds = inst.Cmds
	lb.deps = inst.Deps
	lb.status = inst.Status
	r.makeBallot(replica, instance)

	inst.bal = lb.lastTriedBallot
	inst.vbal = lb.lastTriedBallot
	preply := &PrepareReply{
		r.Id,
		replica,
		instance,
		inst.bal,
		inst.vbal,
		inst.Status,
		inst.Cmds,
		inst.Seq,
		inst.Deps}

	lb.prepareReplies = append(lb.prepareReplies, preply)
	lb.leaderResponded = r.Id == replica

	r.bcastPrepare(replica, instance)

result.summary: Submitted the focused 5-replica probe harness (draft/epaxos/assurance_generated_test.go) as a fixed experiment for the EPaxos recovery value-adoption question, with requirement, verified declaration anchors, prerequisites and two comparisons. The scenario drives X through a real phase-2 acceptance at ballot 0 (accepted by replicas 0, 2, 3), crashes the leader after the Accept broadcast, and recovers instance (0,0) at replica 3, which holds no command for it; it then completes the quiescent exchange. The controller's receipt is still outstanding, so the interpretation remains source-based and conditional, and the reachability gap stays open pending formal execution.
